title: Because, and To
overview: Say why with because and to: I went out to buy bread. Say what you hope to do, what you enjoy, and how you travel. Show all you can do after Level 1, and get ready for Level 2.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 17 words.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read texts 1 and 3. Keep text 2 for the check.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen back.
Writing: plan, write and check. Made-up is OK.
Practice: 1 to 4, then the Level 1 check in 5 and 6.
Quiz: 12 questions on all of Level 1. Last, your portfolio.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 19.
It is the last unit of Level 1.
In this unit, you say why.
Then you look back at all of Level 1.
First, because.
Because gives the reason.
I stayed at home because it rained.
Why did you stay at home? Because it rained.
Say what happened first. Then say because and the reason.
When you write, keep it one sentence.
Do not put a full stop before because.
Say be-cause. The strong part is cause.
Now to, for why you go.
I went to the shop to buy bread.
To the shop tells you where. To buy bread tells you why.
After to, the doing word stays the same: to buy, to get, to see.
For goes with a thing: I went out for bread.
To goes with a doing word: I went out to buy bread.
Now hope and enjoy.
Some words take to next.
I hope to travel. I decided to take the bus. She agreed to help me.
Some words take -ing next.
I enjoy cooking. I avoid going out in a storm. Keep practising.
Hope to go, but enjoy going.
Now how you travel, and what is in it.
By bus. By train. By car.
No the after by. Not: by the bus.
When you walk, say on foot. Not: by foot.
By can also say who made a thing: a photo by Eva.
From tells you where a thing starts: bread from the market.
With: it is in it. Tea with milk.
Without: it is not in it. Coffee without sugar.
Now look back.
In Level 1, you learned the 26 letters and their sounds.
You can say who you are, and ask and answer questions.
You can talk about people, things and places.
You can say what you do every day, and what happened yesterday.
You can follow and give instructions.
You can compare things: bigger, better, the best.
You can read short texts, and write short notes.
And you can join ideas with and, but and because.
To finish Level 1, there are two things.
First, your portfolio. A portfolio is a set of your work in one place.
Choose five things you made in Level 1, from four units or more.
Under each one, write one line. Start it with: This shows I can.
Then make two new recordings: a short talk about a day, and Reading 1 out loud.
Second, the Level 1 check, in Practice 5 and 6.
It has four parts: reading, listening, writing and speaking.
Give each part its own score, out of ten.
Do not add the four scores together.
Your reading and your speaking can be at different levels. That is normal.
The check is practice, not a certificate. It is for you.
When every part is 8 or more, start Level 2.
A part under 8? The answers tell you which units to go back to.
In Level 2, you read longer texts and say more.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

words.meaning: Why a thing happens, or why you do it.
words.example: The reason is simple: the bus was late.
practice: What is the reason?
I have one reason: I was tired.
Give a reason with because.
The rain was the reason we stayed at home.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you did last week. Ask it to ask you: What was the reason? Answer with because.

words.meaning: Want a good thing to happen, and think it can happen.
words.example: I hope to visit my aunt next month.
practice: I hope to finish this unit today.
We hope to see you soon.
He hopes to play in the football team.
What do you hope to do next year?
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things you hope to do, true or made up. Ask it to check that to comes after hope each time.

words.meaning: Think about it, then choose what to do.
words.example: I decided to walk, not take the bus.
practice: We decided to stay at home.
Did you decide to go?
She decided to learn English.
I can't decide: tea or coffee?
words.tutor: Give the tutor two choices, for example the bus or on foot. Ask it which one you should pick, then say: I decided to …

words.meaning: Like a thing very much while you do it.
words.example: I enjoy cooking at the weekend.
practice: Do you enjoy reading?
She enjoys walking in the park.
We enjoyed the film.
I don't enjoy running in the rain.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three things you enjoy doing. Ask it to check each one has -ing. I enjoy swimming, not I enjoy to swim.

words.meaning: Think the same as another person. Or: say yes to a plan.
words.example: I agree with you. The film was very good.
practice: Do you agree?
She agreed to help me.
We agreed to meet at six.
I don't agree. I think the book is better.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three short opinions, like Tea is better than coffee. Say I agree or I don't agree, and give one reason with because.

words.meaning: Stay away from a thing, or not do it, if you can.
words.example: I avoid going out in a storm.
practice: I avoid the busy road.
She avoids drinking coffee at night.
Check your work to avoid mistakes.
We avoid driving in the snow.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you avoid and why. Ask it to check you used -ing after avoid and because for the reason.

words.meaning: Not stop: go on doing it. Also: have a thing and not give it back.
practice: Keep going! You are nearly there.
It kept raining all day.
Keep your ticket. You need it on the train.
I keep forgetting my keys.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor about two lines: Keep your ticket. Keep going. Say which one means do not stop.

words.meaning: A thing you want to do or get, and you work for it.
words.example: My goal is to read a book in English.
practice: What is your goal for next month?
Her goal is to speak English at work.
My goal: ten new words every week.
We have one goal: to finish Level 1.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one goal, true or made up. It can be for school, for work or just for you. Ask it for two small steps to get there.

words.example: I can see my progress: I read faster now.
practice: You made good progress this month.
Look at your first writing and your last one. That is progress.
The check shows your progress in each skill.
How can I check my progress?
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you can do now. Before Level 1, you could not do it. Ask it to help you say it in one sentence.

words.meaning: Get better, or make a thing better.
words.example: My writing improved a lot this year.
practice: How can I improve my speaking?
Listen back to improve.
Her English is improving every week.
I want to improve my spelling.
words.tutor: Record one sentence, then say it again better. Tell the tutor what you changed to improve it.

words.meaning: A thing you can do well, because you learned and practised it.
words.example: Reading, writing, listening and speaking are four skills.
practice: Cooking is a good skill.
Which skill is easy for you?
Driving is a skill you learn.
The Level 1 check looks at each skill on its own.
words.tutor: Name the four skills to the tutor. Ask it which one is easiest for you. Say why, with because.

words.meaning: How far up you are, like the floors of a building.
words.example: This is Level 1. Next is Level 2.
practice: What level is this book?
The next level is harder.
My reading is at a good level.
Your speaking and writing can be at different levels.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: What can a learner do after Level 1? Then ask it one question about Level 2. Short answers only.

words.meaning: The time after now: tomorrow, next year and later.
words.example: In the future, I hope to travel.
practice: What do you want to do in the future?
We can't see the future.
In the future, I will use English at school or at work.
Plan for the future.
words.starter: In the future, I hope to …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things about your future. Use I hope to and I will. True or made up is fine.

words.meaning: Happy about a good thing you did, or a person did.
words.example: I am proud of my work in Level 1.
practice: Are you proud of your writing?
My grandmother is proud of me.
He felt proud when he finished.
I am proud because I can read this now.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you made in Level 1 that you are proud of. Say why, with because.

words.meaning: Sure you can do it well.
words.example: I feel confident when I speak slowly.
practice: Are you confident about the test?
She is a confident driver.
I am not confident yet, but I am improving.
Practice makes you confident.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you feel confident about in English. Then tell it one thing you don't feel confident about yet. Ask it for one tip.

words.meaning: Going from one place to another, often a long way.
words.example: The journey to the city takes two hours by train.
practice: How was your journey?
It was a long journey by bus.
We had a good journey.
The journey on foot takes twenty minutes.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a journey, real or made up. Say where, how and how long. Use by or on foot.

words.meaning: The part at the end of your leg. You stand on it. Two: feet.
words.example: I go to the park on foot.
practice: My foot hurts.
On foot, not by foot.
I have two feet.
It is ten minutes on foot.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor three How do you get to …? questions. Answer with by bus, by car or on foot. Check you never say by foot.

grammar.title: Because: giving the reason
grammar.explanation:
Because answers the question why.
First say what happened. Then say because and the reason.
I stayed at home because it rained.
grammar.rule:
What happened + because + the reason:
I stayed at home because it rained.
I was late because the bus was late.
She is happy because she found her key.
We took a taxi because we had a lot of bags.

Why are you tired?
Because I worked late.

Speaking: Because I worked late. That is OK.
Writing: one sentence, two parts.
I am tired because I worked late.

and: one more thing
but: a different thing
because: the reason
grammar.workedExample:
Two lines: I took a taxi. I was late.
1. Which line is the reason? I was late.
2. Start with what happened: I took a taxi.
3. Add because, then the reason.
4. I took a taxi because I was late.
5. Check: ask why. Why did you take a taxi? Because I was late. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to put a full stop before because.
No: I stayed at home. Because it rained.
Yes: I stayed at home because it rained.
Keep it one sentence, with one full stop at the end.
grammar.tip: Ask why. The answer starts with because.
grammar.practice:
Join the two lines with because.
1. I had some water. I was thirsty.
2. She stayed at home. She was tired.
3. We took the bus. It was raining.
4. He is happy. He found his phone.
5. I called my friend. I wanted to say thanks.
6. I am hungry. I didn't have lunch.
7. Choose the reason: I took an umbrella because (it was raining / it was hot).
8. Answer with because: Why do you study English?
grammar.answers:
1. I had some water because I was thirsty.
2. She stayed at home because she was tired.
3. We took the bus because it was raining.
4. He is happy because he found his phone.
5. I called my friend because I wanted to say thanks.
6. I am hungry because I didn't have lunch.
7. it was raining
8. Your own answer. For example: Because I need it at school or at work.
Wrong on 1 to 6? Check the order: what happened, then because, then the reason.
A full stop before because? Take it out: it is one sentence.

grammar.title: To buy bread: saying why you go
grammar.explanation:
To and a doing word can say why.
I went to the shop to buy bread.
Why did you go? To buy bread.
grammar.rule:
Where + why:
I went to the shop to buy bread.
She went to the bank to get money.
We went to the park to play football.
I called Dan to say sorry.
I study English to read books in English.

Why did you go to the library?
To borrow a book.

to the shop: where
to buy bread: why

After to, the doing word stays the same:
to buy, to get, to see.
Not: to bought. Not: to buying.
grammar.workedExample:
Eva went to the post office. She wanted to send a card.
1. Why did she go? To send a card.
2. The doing word: send.
3. Put to before it: to send a card.
4. Eva went to the post office to send a card.
5. Check: send stays the same after to. Not sent.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to use for here.
No: I went to the shop for buy bread.
Yes: I went to the shop to buy bread.
For goes with a thing: I went to the shop for bread.
To goes with a doing word: to buy bread.
grammar.tip: Where? To the shop. Why? To buy bread.
grammar.practice:
Write to and the word in brackets.
1. I went to the library ___ a book. (borrow)
2. She went to the market ___ some fish. (buy)
3. We went to the station ___ a friend. (meet)
4. He went to the bank ___ money. (get)
5. I use a dictionary ___ new words. (check)
6. Why did you go to the café? ___ a coffee. (have)
7. Choose: I went to the park (for run / to run).
8. Choose: I went to the shop (for / to) bread.
grammar.answers:
1. to borrow  2. to buy  3. to meet  4. to get  5. to check  6. To have  7. to run  8. for
Wrong on 8? Bread is a thing, so for bread. Buy is a doing word, so to buy bread.
Wrong on 7? Run is a doing word: to run, not for run.

grammar.title: Hope to go, enjoy going
grammar.explanation:
Some words take to next: hope, decide, agree.
Some words take -ing next: enjoy, avoid, keep.
Learn them in two groups.
grammar.rule:
To next:
I hope to travel next year.
I decided to take the bus.
She agreed to help me.
I want to learn. I need to go.

-ing next:
I enjoy cooking.
I avoid going out in a storm.
Keep practising every day.
I like reading.

After to, the word stays the same: to go, to see.
For -ing, add -ing: go, going. Swim, swimming.
grammar.workedExample:
Eva / enjoy / swim. Make a sentence.
1. Enjoy is in the -ing group.
2. swim: swimming. Two m.
3. Eva is she, so enjoy takes s: enjoys.
4. Eva enjoys swimming.
5. Check: no to after enjoy. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to put to after enjoy.
No: I enjoy to cook.
Yes: I enjoy cooking.
And -ing after hope:
No: I hope seeing you.
Yes: I hope to see you.
grammar.tip: Hope, decide, agree: to. Enjoy, avoid, keep: -ing.
grammar.practice:
Choose the right words.
1. I hope (to see / seeing) you soon.
2. I enjoy (to walk / walking) in the park.
3. We decided (to stay / staying) at home.
4. She avoids (to drive / driving) at night.
5. He agreed (to help / helping) me.
6. Keep (to try / trying)!
7. I want (to learn / learning) more English.
8. They enjoy (to cook / cooking) together.
grammar.answers:
1. to see  2. walking  3. to stay  4. driving  5. to help  6. trying  7. to learn  8. cooking
Wrong on 2, 4, 6 or 8? Enjoy, avoid and keep take -ing.
Wrong on 1, 3, 5 or 7? Hope, decide, agree and want take to.

grammar.title: By bus, from the city, without sugar
grammar.explanation:
By: how you travel, or who made a thing.
From: where a thing or a person starts.
With: it is in it. Without: it is not in it.
grammar.rule:
By, for travel:
by bus, by train, by car, by taxi, by plane, by bike
Walking? Say on foot. Not by foot.

By, for the person who made it:
a photo by Eva. A song by Dan.

From:
I am from a small town.
This bread is from the market.
The train from the city is late.

With and without:
tea with milk
coffee without sugar
a room with a big window
a room without a window
grammar.workedExample:
Priya goes to the market. She takes the bus. She has tea, but no sugar.
1. How does she go? The bus: by bus.
2. No the after by.
3. Priya goes to the market by bus.
4. No sugar in her tea: without.
5. Priya has tea without sugar.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to add the after by.
No: I go to the market by the bus.
Yes: I go to the market by bus.
Walking is different.
No: I go by foot.
Yes: I go on foot.
grammar.tip: By bus, on foot. With: in it. Without: not in it.
grammar.practice:
Write by, on, from, with or without.
1. I go to the market ___ bus.
2. She walks. She goes ___ foot.
3. This fish is ___ the river.
4. Coffee ___ milk, please. I like milk in it.
5. Tea ___ sugar, please. I don't want sugar.
6. We went to the island ___ plane.
7. It is a photo ___ Tomas. He took it.
8. The bus ___ the city arrives at six.
grammar.answers:
1. by  2. on  3. from  4. with  5. without  6. by  7. by  8. from
Wrong on 2? Walking is on foot, not by foot.
Wrong on 7? By can say who made a thing: a photo by Tomas.

readings.title: A Day at the Lake
readings.setting: A trip to a lake, on one Saturday.
readings.passage:
Last Saturday, I went to the lake with my cousin Dan.
We went by bus, and then on foot for twenty minutes.
We left early because the bus is very slow.
We went there to see the animals and the trees.
The journey was long, but I enjoyed it.
At the lake, we sat under a big tree.
We had hot tea from a flask.
The flask kept the tea hot all day.
Dan took a lot of photos.
I decided to try swimming, but the water was very cold!
I think the lake is the most beautiful place near my town.
I hope to go again next month.

readings.title: How People in One Town Travel
readings.setting: Yara gives a short talk about how people travel. Keep this one for the Level 1 check: in Practice 5, listen to it first, and do not read it.
readings.passage:
Hello. My name is Yara.
Last month, I asked 200 people one question.
How do you get to school or work?
80 people go by bus because it is cheap.
50 people go on foot. They live near their school or work.
40 people go by car, and 30 go by bike.
Many people told me the morning bus is crowded.
There are too many people on it, and you can't sit down.
Some people avoid the bus for that reason.
They leave home early to walk.
I think the town needs more buses in the morning.
I think walking is the best. It is free, and it is good for you.
Thank you for listening.

readings.title: The Menu at the Station Café
readings.setting: The wall of a small café at a bus station.
readings.passage:
THE STATION CAFÉ
Open every day, 6 in the morning to 8 in the evening.
The number after each thing is the price.
DRINKS
Tea with milk: 2
Tea without milk: 2
Coffee: 3
Want sugar? Please ask at the desk.
FOOD
Bread from our kitchen: 1
Egg and rice: 4
Fish from the river, with vegetables: 6
Fruit, without sugar: 3
Please buy a drink or food to sit here.
The bus to the city leaves from door 2.

comprehension.q: How did the writer and Dan get to the lake?
comprehension.a: By bus, and then on foot.
comprehension.why: Line 2: We went by bus, and then on foot for twenty minutes.

comprehension.a: Because the bus is very slow.
comprehension.why: Line 3: We left early because the bus is very slow. Because gives the reason.

comprehension.q: Why did they go to the lake?
comprehension.a: To see the animals and the trees.
comprehension.why: Line 4: We went there to see the animals and the trees. To see tells you why.

comprehension.q: What is a flask? Look at the words near it.
comprehension.a: A bottle that keeps a drink hot.
comprehension.why: Lines 7 and 8: hot tea from a flask. The flask kept the tea hot all day.

comprehension.q: What does the writer think about the lake?
comprehension.a: It is the most beautiful place near the writer's town.
comprehension.why: Line 11: I think the lake is the most beautiful place near my town. I think tells you what the writer thinks.

comprehension.q: Did the writer swim for a long time? Why?
comprehension.a: No, not for long. The water was very cold.
comprehension.why: Line 10: I decided to try swimming, but the water was very cold! But tells you it did not go well.

comprehension.q: You want tea, but you don't like milk. What do you ask for, and what is the price?
comprehension.a: Tea without milk. The price is 2.
comprehension.why: The menu says: Tea without milk: 2. Without means no milk in it.

comprehension.q: You want sugar in your coffee. What must you do?
comprehension.why: The menu says: Want sugar? Please ask at the desk.
The menu says: Fish from the river, with vegetables. From tells you where it starts.

comprehension.q: You are in the café. Your bus to the city leaves soon. Which door do you go to?
comprehension.why: The last line says: The bus to the city leaves from door 2.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Why? Because
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
Why are you tired? Because I worked late.
Why did you take a taxi? Because I was late.
I stayed at home because it rained.
I had some water because I was thirsty.
Say be-cause. The strong part is cause.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: because in each line? No stop before because in lines 3 and 4?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor five Why questions about a day. Answer each one with because and a reason, true or made up.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Why did you go?
speaking.instructions:
Read the question. Say the answer with to.
1. Why did you go to the bank? To get money.
2. Why did you go to the library? To borrow a book.
3. Why did you go to the station? To meet a friend.
4. Why did you go to the market? To buy some fruit.
Now say 2 full lines. For example: I went to the market to buy some fruit.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 answers, then your 2 full lines.
Tap again. Listen.
Check: to before each doing word? Get, borrow, meet and buy stay the same?
speaking.tutor: Name four places to the tutor. Ask it to ask you why you went to each one. Answer with to and a doing word.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — What do you enjoy doing?
speaking.instructions:
Read the friend's line. Say your line.
1. Friend: What do you enjoy doing? You: I enjoy cooking and reading.
2. Friend: What do you hope to do next year? You: I hope to travel.
3. Friend: What do you avoid? You: I avoid going out in a storm.
4. Friend: Did you decide to take the bus? You: No, I decided to walk.
5. Now ask your friend back: And you? What do you enjoy doing?
Tap the mic. Say your lines and your question.
Tap again. Listen.
Now say your lines again with your own answers. True or made up is fine.
Check: -ing after enjoy and avoid? To after hope and decide?
A friend can read the friend's lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask you what you enjoy, avoid and hope to do. Answer each one, then ask it the same question back.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — A short talk about a day
speaking.instructions:
Listen to Tomas's talk.
Last Saturday, I went to the market by bus.
I went there to buy fruit and vegetables.
Then I met my friend at a café.
I had tea without sugar. I don't like sugar.
In the afternoon, we walked in the park.
I enjoyed it because the weather was warm.
I hope to go again next week.
Now give your talk about one day. It can be true or made up.
Say 6 lines: where, how, why, what you had, how you felt, a hope.
Tap the mic. Talk. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 6 lines? Past words like went, had and met? Because one time? To for why one time?
speaking.tutor: Give the tutor your talk. Ask it to ask you two questions about your day, and answer them with because or to.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — At the station café
speaking.instructions:
You are at the station café. Look at Reading 3.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! What can I get you?
You: Tea without milk, please.
Desk: With sugar or without?
You: Without, please.
Desk: Food too? Our bread is from our kitchen.
You: Yes, the bread, please. What is the price?
Desk: That is 3, please.
You: Here you are. Thanks!
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: with or without in 2 lines? Please in 2 lines?
Now say it again. Order coffee with milk, and the fish.
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be the person at the café desk. Order a drink and some food from Reading 3, with or without milk or sugar.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Read it out loud: A Day at the Lake
speaking.instructions:
Listen to Reading 1.
Then read it out loud, one line at a time.
Say because as be-cause. The strong part is cause.
Say to short and soft in to see and to go.
Stop a little at each full stop.
Tap the mic. Read all 12 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: all 12 lines? Can you hear every word? A stop at each full stop?
Keep this recording. It can go in your portfolio.
speaking.tutor: Read two lines from Reading 1 to the tutor. Ask it which word was hard to hear, then read that line again.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Four reasons
writing.prompt:
Write 4 sentences with because.
Say why you did 4 things last week.
They can be true or made up.
writing.model:
I went to bed early because I was tired.
I took an umbrella because it was raining.
I called my aunt because I wanted to say thanks.
I had a lot of water because it was hot.
writing.criteria:
4 sentences, each with because.
What happened first, then because, then the reason.
No full stop before because.
A capital letter to start each one. A full stop to end it.
writing.support:
Write the 4 reasons first, one word each: tired, raining, thanks, hot.
Then write what you did before each one.
Join each pair with because.
writing.extension: Add one line with but: I was tired, but I finished my homework.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A note: where I went, and why
writing.prompt:
Write a note to a friend or someone in your family.
Say where you went today and why. Use to.
Names and places can be made up.
writing.model:
Hi Ana,
I went to the market to buy fruit.
Then I went to the post office to send your card.
Now I am at the library to borrow a book.
See you at six.
Ivan
writing.criteria:
A name at the top and your name at the end.
3 lines with to and a doing word, for why.
The doing word after to stays the same: to buy, not to bought.
A capital letter for each name.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the places and the things.
Check each to: is a doing word next?
writing.extension: Add one line with because: I went early because the shop closes at five.

writing.title: Writing 3 — Hopes, and things I enjoy
writing.prompt:
Write 5 lines about you.
Use enjoy, avoid, decided to, my goal is to and hope to.
True or made up is fine.
writing.model:
I enjoy walking in the park.
I avoid going out in a storm.
Last year I decided to learn English.
My goal is to read a book in English.
I hope to start Level 2 soon.
writing.criteria:
5 lines.
-ing after enjoy and avoid.
To after decided, is and hope.
A capital letter and a full stop in each line.
writing.support:
Start with the two -ing lines: I enjoy … . I avoid … .
Then the three to lines.
Check each line with the tip on Pattern 3.
writing.extension: Add a reason to one line: I enjoy walking because it is free.

writing.title: Writing 4 — Plan, write and check: a day out
writing.prompt:
Write about a day out. It can be true or made up.
First plan: write 5 notes. Where? How? Why? What happened? How did you feel?
Then write 6 sentences from your notes.
Last, check with the list.
writing.model:
Plan: park. On foot. To play football. Rain! Happy.
Last Sunday, I went to the park on foot.
I went there to play football with my friends.
Then it started to rain, but we kept playing.
After that, we had lunch at a café.
I had rice and fish, and tea with milk.
I felt happy because it was a good day.
writing.criteria:
5 notes, then 6 sentences.
Past words: went, had, felt.
One line with because. One line with to for why.
One line with by, on foot, with or without.
A capital letter to start each one. A full stop to end it.
Clear letters: a space between each two words.
writing.support:
Write your 5 notes as one or two words each.
Turn each note into one sentence.
The model shows how: park becomes I went to the park on foot.
writing.extension: Read your text out loud and record it. It can go in your portfolio.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Join with because
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 6 with a to f. Then write each line with because.
1. I took a taxi
2. She stayed at home
3. We ate at a café
4. He took an umbrella
5. I am learning English
6. They are happy
a. it was raining.
b. the fridge was empty.
c. I was late.
d. they found the key.
e. she was tired.
f. I need it at school or at work.
activities.answers:
1c: I took a taxi because I was late.
2e: She stayed at home because she was tired.
3b: We ate at a café because the fridge was empty.
4a: He took an umbrella because it was raining.
5f: I am learning English because I need it at school or at work.
6d: They are happy because they found the key.
Check 2 and 6: she goes with she, and they goes with they.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud with because. Write it. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Where and why
activities.instructions:
Match the place with why. Then write the line.
For example: I went to the library to borrow a book.
1. the library
2. the chemist
3. the station
4. the bank
5. the post office
6. the market
7. the park
8. the café
a. to send a postcard
b. to buy vegetables
c. to borrow a book
d. to catch a train
e. to get money
f. to buy soap
g. to have a coffee
h. to play football
activities.answers:
1c  2f  3d  4e  5a  6b  7h  8g
For example: I went to the chemist to buy soap.
Check: to before each doing word, and the doing word stays the same.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud: I went to … to … . Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — To or -ing?
activities.instructions:
Write the word in brackets with to or with -ing.
1. I hope ___ you next week. (see)
2. She enjoys ___ in the morning. (run)
3. We decided ___ the train. (take)
4. Avoid ___ on the phone when you cross the road. (talk)
5. He agreed ___ me with my homework. (help)
6. Keep ___! You are nearly there. (go)
7. I want ___ to Level 2. (go)
8. Do you enjoy ___? (dance)
9. My goal is ___ a book in English. (read)
10. They avoid ___ in the rain. (drive)
activities.answers:
1. to see  2. running  3. to take  4. talking  5. to help  6. going  7. to go  8. dancing  9. to read  10. driving
The hard ones: 2 (two n) and 8 (drop the e).
Wrong on 9? My goal is: to comes next.
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Write the word. Check each letter with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — By, from, with, without, and the new words
activities.instructions:
Part A. Write by, on, from, with or without.
1. I go to the city ___ train.
2. It is near. We can go ___ foot.
3. Coffee ___ sugar, please. I don't want sugar.
4. These apples are ___ my garden.
5. Tea ___ milk, please. I like milk in it.
6. It is a song ___ Yara. She made it.
Part B. Write the word: goal, progress, improve, skill, level, future, proud, confident.
7. You did good work. You feel ___.
8. This is ___ 1. Next is 2.
9. Reading is one ___. Speaking is another.
10. A thing you want to do, and you work for it: a ___.
11. I am sure I can do it. I feel ___.
12. Tomorrow, next year and later: the ___.
13. Getting better, step by step: ___.
14. Get better, or make a thing better: ___.
activities.answers:
Part A: 1. by  2. on  3. without  4. from  5. with  6. by
Part B: 7. proud  8. Level  9. skill  10. goal  11. confident  12. future  13. progress  14. improve
Wrong on 2? Walking is on foot, never by foot.
Check 7 and 11: proud is about work you did. Confident is about work you are going to do.
12 to 14 right: good.
11 or less: read Pattern 4 and the Words page, then do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud with your word. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — The Level 1 check: reading and listening
activities.instructions:
This is the Level 1 check, Parts A and B.
Score each part on its own, out of 10.

Part A. Reading. Read the note. Then answer 1 to 10.
A NOTE ON THE FRIDGE
Mia,
I went out early to buy fish for dinner.
Then I went to the chemist by bus, to get soap.
Your brother called at nine.
His train from the city was late because it snowed.
He is coming here by taxi.
Please don't eat the apples. They are for him.
I think the new café on our street is very good.
The coffee is cheap and the bread is warm.
But it is noisy: loud music all day!
Back at six.
Eva
1. Why did Eva go out early?
2. How did she go to the chemist?
3. Why did she go to the chemist?
4. Where is the train from?
5. Why was the train late?
6. How is Mia's brother coming?
7. Who are the apples for?
8. What does Eva think of the new café?
9. What does noisy mean? Look at the words near it.
10. Yes or no: Eva is back at nine.

Part B. Listening.
Go to Reading 2, How People in One Town Travel. Tap Listen.
Do not read the words. Look away while you listen.
Listen two times. Then answer 1 to 10.
1. How many people did Yara ask?
2. What was her question?
3. How many people go by bus?
4. Why do they go by bus?
5. How many people go on foot?
6. What does crowded mean? Think about the words near it.
7. Why do some people avoid the bus?
8. Why do they leave home early?
9. What does Yara think the town needs?
10. What does Yara think is the best way to travel, and why?
activities.answers:
Part A, Reading:
1. To buy fish for dinner.  2. By bus.  3. To get soap.  4. From the city.  5. Because it snowed.  6. By taxi.  7. For Mia's brother.  8. It is very good. (I think tells you it is what Eva thinks.)  9. Loud, with a lot of sound.  10. No. She is back at six. Nine is when the brother called.
Part B, Listening:
1. 200 people.  2. How do you get to school or work?  3. 80.  4. Because it is cheap.  5. 50.  6. Too many people, and you can't sit down.  7. It is crowded in the morning.  8. To walk.  9. More buses in the morning.  10. Walking, because it is free and good for you.
Score Part A and Part B on their own. Do not add them.
Reading, Part A:
8 to 10: your reading is working at A1.
5 to 7: nearly there. Go back to the Reading texts in Units 14 to 18, and answer their questions again.
0 to 4: go back to the Reading texts in Units 7 to 13 first. Read each one out loud, then do its questions.
Listening, Part B:
8 to 10: your listening is working at A1.
5 to 7: nearly there. In Units 14 to 18, listen to each reading with your eyes closed, then read it.
0 to 4: go back to the lessons in Units 7 to 13 first. Listen and repeat each line.
activities.solo: Do Part A with the note in front of you. For Part B, only listen: do not read Reading 2 first. Write your answers on paper. Check with the key and count.

activities.title: Practice 6 — The Level 1 check: writing and speaking
activities.instructions:
This is the Level 1 check, Parts C and D.
Score each part on its own, out of 10.

Part C. Writing.
Write about last weekend. It can be true or made up.
Plan first: 5 notes. Then write 6 to 8 sentences.
Wait ten minutes. Then check your text with this list.
One point for each yes.
1. 6 sentences or more?
2. A capital letter at the start of every sentence?
3. A full stop or a question mark at the end of every sentence?
4. 3 past words or more, all of them right? (went, had, saw)
5. One line with because and a reason?
6. One line with to for why? (to buy, to see)
7. One line joined with and or but?
8. One line with by, on foot, from, with or without?
9. 5 words checked in a dictionary, and all 5 spelled right?
10. Clear letters: every letter easy to read, and a space between each two words?

Part D. Speaking.
Tap the mic and talk. Your answers can be true or made up.
Say hello and your name. A made-up name is fine.
Say 4 sentences about last weekend.
Answer: What do you hope to do next year? Why?
Answer: What do you enjoy doing?
Say goodbye.
Tap the mic again. Listen back.
One point for each yes.
1. Hello, your name and goodbye?
2. 4 sentences about the weekend?
3. Past words for the weekend, all of them right?
4. One line with because?
5. Hope to, with to after hope?
6. Enjoy with -ing after it?
7. And or but to join two ideas?
8. No long stop: never a stop longer than you can count to three?
9. You can write down every word you hear on the recording?
10. Because said as be-cause, with the strong part on cause?
activities.answers:
There is no one right text or talk. Your list gives the score.
Score Part C and Part D on their own. Do not add them.
Writing, Part C:
8 to 10: your writing is working at A1.
5 to 7: nearly there. For each no, go back:
A no on 1, 2 or 3: Unit 13.
On 4: Units 10 and 16.
On 5 or 6: this unit, Patterns 1 and 2.
On 7: Units 4 and 13.
On 8: this unit, Pattern 4.
On 9: Unit 13, the planning and checking.
On 10: Unit 0, the letters.
0 to 4: go back to Units 10 and 13 first. Then do Part C again.
Speaking, Part D:
8 to 10: your speaking is working at A1.
5 to 7: nearly there. A no on 3: Units 10 and 16. On 4 to 6: this unit, Patterns 1 and 3. On 7: Units 4 and 13. On 8 to 10: do the Speaking tasks in Units 14 to 18 again. Record, listen back, record again.
0 to 4: go back to the Speaking tasks in Units 7 and 10 first. Then do Part D again.
Now look at your four scores, A to D.
Do not add them up into one number. They are four skills.
Your reading, writing, listening and speaking can be at different levels. That is normal.
This check is practice, not a certificate. It is for you, to see your progress.
Every skill 8 or more? Start Level 2.
One skill under 8? Go back to the units for that skill. Then do that part again.
activities.solo: Wait ten minutes before you check your writing. Then read it slowly, one line at a time. Keep the list next to it. Listen to your recording two times: first for the words, then for the list.

quizzes.q: I took a taxi ___ I was late.
quizzes.why: Because gives the reason: I was late. But is for a different thing, and I was late is not different. To and for do not join two sentences like this.

quizzes.q: I went to the bank ___ money.
quizzes.why: Why did you go? To get money. For goes with a thing, not a doing word. After to, get stays the same, so not to got. Getting does not say why here.
Enjoy takes -ing: I enjoy walking. To walk is the tempting one. But to goes after hope and decide, not enjoy. Walk and walked are not right after enjoy.

quizzes.q: I don't take the bus. I walk. I go ___.
quizzes.why: Walking is on foot. By foot is a very common mistake. By the bus has the, and you walk, so there is no bus. With foot is not right.

quizzes.q: I don't want sugar. Coffee ___ sugar, please.
quizzes.why: Without: it is not in it. With means you want sugar in it. By is for travel or for who made a thing. From tells you where a thing starts.

quizzes.q: You finished all of Level 1. You feel ___ of your work.
quizzes.why: Proud: happy about a good thing you did. Afraid and angry are not happy feelings. Late is about time, not a feeling.
From an earlier unit: yesterday is the past, and go changes to went. Go and goes are for now or every day. Going needs am, is or was in front.

quizzes.q: She ___ at a café every Saturday.
quizzes.why: From an earlier unit: every Saturday is a routine. With she, add s: she works. Work has no s. Working needs is in front. Is work is not right.

quizzes.q: The train is ___ than the bus.
quizzes.why: From an earlier unit: two things with than, so fast becomes faster. Fastest is for the most of three or more. More fast is not right: a short word takes -er.
From an earlier unit: Have you ever takes the past form, climbed. Climb and climbs are for now. Climbing needs are or were, not have.
From an earlier unit: a question with she and live takes does. Do is for I, you, we and they. Is and are go with -ing: Is she living here?

options: I go to the market on monday.
i go to the market on Monday.
I go to the market on Monday.
I go to the Market on Monday.
quizzes.a: I go to the market on Monday.
quizzes.why: From an earlier unit: I and day names take a capital letter. The first line has a small m on Monday. The second has a small i. Market is not a name, so it needs no capital.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a checklist the learner can see. The Level 1 check in Practices 5 and 6 is scored by the learner against countable points, so it needs no marker. If you are helping, listen to the Part D recording with the checklist in front of you, and let the learner do the counting.

teacherNotes.type: The Level 1 check: four skills, never one grade
teacherNotes.note: Reading (Part A, a new note) and listening (Part B, which plays Reading 2) are scored out of ten from the key; writing (Part C) and speaking (Part D) out of ten from ten yes-or-no points. Each skill has its own bands: 8 to 10 working at A1, 5 to 7 nearly there, 0 to 4 go back first, each naming units to revisit, and the writing and speaking keys map each missed point to the unit that teaches it. Do not add or average the four: a learner who reads at 9 and speaks at 6 has two facts, not one middling number. It is practice, not a certificate. The plan makes it the entry condition for Level 2, which the key states as every skill at 8 or more. Reading 2 is reserved for the listening part, so it has no comprehension questions in the Reading section; ask the learner to hear it before reading it.

teacherNotes.type: The portfolio is marked on all eight criteria
teacherNotes.note: The assignment is marked on all eight rubric criteria, so the instructions make sure each one has something to mark. Pronunciation and Fluency come from the two new recordings; Interaction from the role-play the learner must include; Accuracy, Range and Purpose from the written pieces; Understanding from the Part B answers; Real-world documents from the form, card or note. The learner chooses the pieces: five or more, from four units or more, each with a This shows I can line under it. Those lines matter most. A learner who can name what a piece shows has done the looking back that the source unit did at a school showcase.

Four slips to listen for. A full stop before because, which leaves Because it rained. alone on a line; in speech a short answer like that is fine, in writing it is not. For with a doing word: for buy bread (for bread and to buy bread are both right). To after enjoy: I enjoy to cook. And by foot or by the bus. Each key names the slip, so point at the key rather than at the error.

So for results, in order to, like to beside like -ing, and by in passive sentences all come later; this unit uses by only for travel and for who made a thing. Journey is used only for real travel, never for the learner's learning, and goal, progress, level and future are about school, work or the learner's own plans, never assumed. No task asks for real personal details, and the AI tutor is a rehearsal partner: no score in this unit comes from it.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say why with because.
I can write why I went: to buy bread.
I can say what I hope to do and enjoy doing.
I can say by bus, on foot, with milk, without sugar.
I can read a short text and find what the writer thinks.
I can listen to a short talk and say what it is about.
I can plan, write and check six sentences.
I can give a short talk about my day.

assignment.title: My Level 1 portfolio
assignment.instructions:
A portfolio is a set of your work in one place.
Part 1. Choose 5 things you made in Level 1, or more.
They must come from 4 different units, or more.
They can be Writing tasks or Speaking recordings.
In your 5, put:
one role-play, where you answer and ask back,
one form, card or note: for example, from Unit 4 or Unit 10,
and your answers to Part B of the Level 1 check.
Under each one, write one line: This shows I can …
For example: This shows I can ask for a thing in a shop.
Part 2. Make 2 new recordings.
1. A short talk about a day, true or made up, like Speaking 4.
2. Reading 1 out loud, like Speaking 6.
You can use made-up names and details.
assignment.submissionType: Written work and audio recordings, each with a This shows I can line
